source.title: On the Beilinson–Bloch–Kato conjecture for Rankin–Selberg motives
source.authors: Yifeng Liu, Yichao Tian, Liang Xiao, Wei Zhang, Xinwen Zhu
readSections: Entire published paper, §§1–8 and Appendices A–D
Targeted original prerequisite sections; see readLedger

summary: Continuation of PR #2181: Partial extraction and routing of the integral unitary level-raising and two-reciprocity-law proof of conditional Bloch–Kato rank zero and one. It retains the exact main hypothesis boundary, records source repairs and open proof gates, reuses existing PEL/trace proposals and provides a consumer-derived API/test specification for every included definition or construction. It is not a claim of full census, proof closure or formalization.

contexts.coefficients: F/F+ is the source CM/totally-real extension with its chosen embedding, conjugation c, CM type and reflex field. Eλ is a finite extension of Qell, Oλ its valuation ring, λ a uniformizer. Rbar(m)=R/λ^m. Arithmetic Frobenius and Qell(1) of Hodge–Tate weight −1 are used. q is residue cardinality in Appendices B–C; p is the selected rational prime in the Shimura-model sections. Do not silently identify these in general local fields.
contexts.ranks: For the main theorems n≥2 and n0,n1 are respectively the even and odd members of {n,n+1}; n0=2r0, n1=2r1+1 and r0+r1=n. The tensor is Rλ(Π0)⊗Rλ(Π1)(n). Section 2’s auxiliary tensor lemmas have their own more general rank assumptions.
contexts.geometricSetup: The unitary model items retain the standard definite/indefinite hermitian data, neat levels, the reflex/type condition, coefficient invertibility and moduli conditions of §§3.3–5.2. A locator with bundled parts is explicitly provisional in this partial extraction; it is not an exact completed Lean signature.
contexts.hypothesisBoundary: Hypothesis 3.2.10 is retained in both ranks. The paper states the small-rank results and cites future work in the general case; no general closure is claimed. Conjecture 8.3.1 and Abel–Jacobi injectivity are not theorem inputs supplied by the library. The 2025 survey’s categorical Conjecture 10.8 remains conjectural.
contexts.statusMeaning: Library means the exact narrow declaration was read at the pinned commit. Planned means existing layer scope supplies the stated interface, not that it is proved. Missing may be routed as a source refinement in an existing layer or as an extension. Explicit proof-obligation items do not assert false printed statements as theorems.

items.name: Continuous first cohomology
items.statement: For a topological group acting continuously on a topological abelian group M, H1 is continuous crossed homomorphisms modulo principal crossed homomorphisms.
items.note: The pinned H1 is an additive quotient. Its pointwise quotient topology is not the canonical discrete-cohomology topology; DiscreteH1 is a separate definition.

api.name: RankinSelberg.ContinuousFirstCohomology.compatibility

unitTests.name: RankinSelberg.ContinuousFirstCohomology.test2

items.name: Trivial-action continuous H1
items.statement: If every g acts trivially on M, H1(G,M) is additively isomorphic to continuous homomorphisms G→Multiplicative M.

items.name: Continuous inflation–restriction exactness
items.statement: For a topological group G, a normal subgroup N and a topological additive group M with continuous distributive G-action, with the quotient/invariant action used by the pinned declaration, range(explicitInfl1)=ker(explicitRes1). Only this exactness at H1 is imported, not a full Hochschild–Serre spectral sequence.

items.statement: Mod(F,O) consists of finitely generated O-modules with their natural ell-adic topology and continuous GF-action; the free subcategory is distinguished. V=R⊗O E and Rbar(m)=R/λ^mR.

items.name: Weak semisimplicity
items.statement: For a procyclic action, M is weakly semisimple if the natural map M^Γ→M_Γ is an isomorphism.

items.name: Procyclic invariants and coinvariants
items.statement: For a finitely generated module over a noetherian coefficient ring, zero procyclic coinvariants imply zero invariants; surjectivity of invariants→coinvariants implies it is an isomorphism.

items.name: Integral weak semisimplicity criterion
items.statement: For a finite free O-module with procyclic action, if its residual representation is weakly semisimple and the generic invariant dimension is at least the residual invariant dimension, the dimensions coincide and the integral representation is weakly semisimple.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.statement: expλ(x,M)=min{a≥0:λ^a x=0}, with infinity if no such a; ordλ(x,M)=sup{a≥0:x∈λ^aM}.

items.statement: For residue characteristic different from ell, H1_ns(K,R)=ker(H1(K,R)→H1(IK,R)); H1_sing is the image of restriction, identified with H1(IK,R)^Gκ when inflation–restriction supplies this identification.

items.name: Unramified local Tate orthogonality
items.statement: For finite torsion dual Galois modules at w not dividing ell, the nonsingular local subgroups annihilate one another under the perfect local Tate pairing; the resulting nonsingular/singular pairing is perfect.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Fontaine–Laffaille crystalline torsion modules
items.statement: For unramified local fields at ell and interval [a,b] in the stated small-weight range, the torsion crystalline category consists of quotients of stable lattices in crystalline representations of that Hodge–Tate range; its nonsingular H1 consists of crystalline extensions by the coefficient module.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

api.statement: Keep extension classes, weights and quotient lattices.

api.name: RankinSelberg.FontaineLaffailleCrystallineTorsionModules.compatibility

unitTests.name: RankinSelberg.FontaineLaffailleCrystallineTorsionModules.test2

items.name: Integral finite condition and torsion crystallinity
items.statement: For a≤0≤b and b−a≤ell−2, the inverse image in H1(K,R) of the torsion crystalline condition on R/λ^m is the integral Bloch–Kato finite condition.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Different-valued crystalline orthogonality
items.statement: If a<0≤b and b−a≤(ell−2)/2, the pairing of the paper’s nonsingular crystalline local conditions on dual torsion lattices lies in D_(E/Qell)^−1/O, inside E/O. It need not be zero over a ramified coefficient field.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Evaluation extension cut out by Selmer classes
items.statement: For S⊂H1(F,Rbar(m)), restrict cocycles to the field F(m) cut out by Rbar(m), and let FS be the common kernel field. Evaluation gives an injective additive θS:Gal(FS/F(m))→HomO(S,Rbar(m)).
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

api.statement: Evaluate θS(g)(s) using any cocycle representative of s.

api.name: RankinSelberg.EvaluationExtensionCutOutBySelmerClasses.characterisation
api.statement: After restriction the action is trivial, so evaluation is independent of coboundaries.

api.name: RankinSelberg.EvaluationExtensionCutOutBySelmerClasses.compatibility

unitTests.name: RankinSelberg.EvaluationExtensionCutOutBySelmerClasses.test2

items.name: Uniform saturation error
items.statement: For generic absolutely irreducible R choose rR as in Lemma 2.3.3 controlling saturation of stable submodules and the scalar/endomorphism error at every torsion exponent. Let f(0)=f(1)=1, f(r+1)=2(f(r)+1) for r≥1.

api.statement: Use one rR for all m and f(r) for the rank of S.

api.name: RankinSelberg.UniformSaturationError.characterisation

api.name: RankinSelberg.UniformSaturationError.compatibility

unitTests.name: RankinSelberg.UniformSaturationError.test2

items.name: Bloch–Kato lattice and propagated finite conditions
items.statement: H1_f(F,V) is the kernel of the global-to-local Bloch–Kato quotient map; H1_f(F,R) is its inverse image. H1_f,R(F,Rbar(m)) is the image of H1_f(F,R), rather than the unrestricted torsion Selmer group.

unitTests.name: RankinSelberg.BlochKatoLatticeAndPropagatedFiniteConditions.test2

items.name: Integral finite classes at local places
items.statement: A class in the propagated finite condition is nonsingular at unramified places away from ell and crystalline nonsingular at ell when the source’s FL interval hypotheses hold.

items.name: Finite free Selmer lattices

items.name: Uniform annihilation at finitely many bad places
items.statement: If V is pure of weight −1 and conjugate self-dual with twist one, then for any finite set Σ away from ell there is mΣ, independent of m, annihilating all localized Rbar(m)-classes at places of Σ. Use vanishing of rational H0,H2 and the local Euler characteristic.

items.statement: GN=(GLN×Gm)⋊{1,c}, c(g,mu)c=(mu g^−t,mu), with multiplier ν(g,mu)=mu and ν(c)=−1 for the quadratic CM case.

items.name: j-polarization
items.statement: A j-polarization of R is a GF-isomorphism Φ:Rc→R∨(j) with Φ^(c,∨)(j)=(−1)^(muΦ+j+1)Φ for a parity muΦ.

items.name: Associated prime and abundant tuple
items.statement: A γ-associated prime has arithmetic Frobenius γ in F(m)+/F+, avoids ell and ramification, and is unramified in FS. A tuple is abundant when its joint evaluation image contains λ^(m0+f(r)rR)(Rbar(m)^hγ)^r, where S is free O/λ^(m−m0) of rank r.

unitTests.name: RankinSelberg.AssociatedPrimeAndAbundantTuple.test2

items.name: Frobenius lifting requires an additional compatibility condition
items.statement: To identify associated-prime evaluations with all hγ-invariant evaluations, prove surjectivity of the appropriate norm/power map in the Galois closure of FS over F+. Prime-to-ell order of γ alone does not suffice; E1 gives a counterexample to the general printed Lemma 2.6.4. The main GI(T²−1) application remains a separately recorded repair request.

items.name: Conditional abundance supply
items.statement: If the restriction map is injective, V is absolutely irreducible, Rbar(m)^hγ is free rank one and the corrected Frobenius-lifting input S23 holds, the saturation bound supplies abundant tuples. The original statement omits the extra lifting justification.

items.name: Diagonal evaluations after a bounded-index shrink
items.statement: An abundant evaluation matrix need not admit a domain basis with off-diagonal evaluations zero. Over a DVR one can instead pass to a bounded-index submodule using the adjugate or a Smith decomposition, tracking the lost λ-exponent. Recovering the exact rank-two Selmer argument with its distinguished first class is an open repair.

items.name: Rankin–Selberg tensor and GI condition
items.statement: Take ranks n0=2r0 and n1=2r1+1, (1−α)-polarized lattices Rα, and R=R0⊗R1. GI^m_(F′,P) requires a simultaneous odd-coset image (γ0,γ1,ξ) on GF′ with prime-to-ell γα orders, P(ξ) a unit, invariant kernels for hγ0,hγ1,hγ0⊗hγ1 all free rank one, no residual −1 eigenvalue on hγ0 and no residual −ξ on hγ1.

items.name: Common-power lift of residual GI
items.statement: GI^1 implies GI^m by raising an arbitrary joint lift to a single ell-power congruent to one modulo all residual prime-to-ell orders and killing all pro-ell parts; preserve ξ as well. Averaging idempotents lift the three rank-one invariant spaces.

items.name: Large-image symmetric-power examples: scalar
items.statement: For geometrically non-CM, geometrically nonisogenous elliptic curves A0,A1/F+, the residual tensor of the specified symmetric powers and twists contains a nontrivial scalar for all sufficiently large ell.

items.name: Large-image symmetric-power examples: irreducibility
items.statement: Under S28’s hypotheses, both residual symmetric-power factors and their tensor are absolutely irreducible for all sufficiently large ell.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Large-image symmetric-power examples: GI
items.statement: Under S28’s hypotheses, for every fixed totally real finite Galois F′/F+ and every NONZERO P∈Z[T], GI^1_(F′,P) holds for all sufficiently large ell. The nonzero premise repairs E4; the application uses P=T²−1.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Relevant cuspidal representation
items.statement: Π of GLN(AF) is relevant when cuspidal, conjugate self-dual and with the precise archimedean characters arg^(1−N),arg^(3−N),…,arg^(N−1).
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Abstract unitary Satake parameter
items.statement: At an inert place a multiset α of N elements has polynomial Pα(T)=∏(T−αi) and is unitary if Pα(T)=(−T)^N Pα(T^−1). At a split place use two multisets with reciprocal polynomials up to a unit.

items.name: Tate-generic parameter
items.statement: For odd N and unit q, the reciprocal monic polynomial P is Tate generic when P′(1) is a unit.

items.name: Intertwining-generic parameter
items.statement: For odd N require P(−q) a unit; for even N require P(−1) a unit.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Level-raising-special parameter
items.statement: For even N require P(q)=0 and P′(q) a unit. In the applications q²−1 is also a unit, so the reciprocal pair q,q^−1 consists of distinct simple roots.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Hermitian space and adjoining a unit line
items.statement: Over OF⊗OF+ B, take a finite projective rank-N module with a perfect pairing linear in the first and conjugate-linear in the second variable. U(V) is its isometry group and V♯=V⊥B·1 with norm(1)=1.

items.name: Spherical Hecke evaluation
items.statement: Use the q-half-normalized Satake map for UN,v with unit 1K. For a parameter over a field with reciprocal ordering, evaluate the torus character algebra and restrict to spherical invariants. Over general rings use coefficient descent or include actual reciprocal-root data; the printed global ordering is not automatic (E5).

items.name: Standard automorphic unitary pair
items.statement: A pair (V, π), with V a hermitian space over F and π a discrete automorphic representation of U(V)(A_{F^+}), is a standard pair if either (1) V is standard definite and π^∞ appears in lim_K C[Sh(V, K)], or (2) V is standard indefinite and π^∞ appears in lim_K ι_ℓ^{-1} H^i_ét(Sh(V, K)_{F̄}, Q̄_ℓ) for the relevant degree i.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Strong coefficient field
items.statement: A coefficient field E is strong for Π when the source’s E-valued Galois realization and all embedding compatibilities in Definition 3.2.3 hold, retaining local Frobenius polynomials and coefficient embeddings.

items.statement: For a relevant Π and its strong coefficient field, ρΠ,λ has the source’s unramified and Frobenius-semisimple WD compatibility with rec(Π|det|^((1−N)/2)), and ρΠ,λ^c≅ρΠ,λ∨(1−N).

items.statement: For the standard indefinite unitary representation π with relevant base change and irreducible ρ, Hypothesis 3.2.10 identifies its degree-(N−1) multiplicity-space Galois representation with ρ^c in the paper’s normalization. This is an explicit hypothesis for the general results, not an unconditional extraction theorem.

items.name: Special and very special inert primes
items.statement: A special inert prime is the degree-one unramified odd rational-prime place used in §3.3, inert in F; the very special condition additionally splits the reflex-field extension specified there. Keep the chosen CM type and the equality QpΦ=Qp² as separate geometry hypotheses.

items.name: OF-abelian object and signature
items.statement: An abelian scheme with OF-action up to prime-to-p isogeny, polarization compatible with conjugation and specified determinant polynomial has its de Rham and Lie modules decomposed by embeddings; the signature records their ranks.

items.statement: The OF-linear p-isogenies used in §§4–5 correspond to F,V-stable Dieudonné lattices with the stated degree/polarization constraints; infinitesimal lifts correspond to orthogonal Hodge filtrations by Grothendieck–Messing and Serre–Tate. The four F/V inclusions and determinant ranks must be verified for each construction.

items.name: Auxiliary CM torus model
items.statement: The fixed rank-one CM moduli scheme T is finite étale at the admitted p, with its finite torus-component action. Product moduli compare with Sh(U(V))×T; take T-invariants using the actual orbit trace, without dividing by the order of the component group.

items.statement: For the §4.1 unramified special-prime PEL datum and neat tame level, Mp parametrizes (A0,i0,λ0;A,i,λ;level) with A p-principally polarized of signature NΦ−τ+τc and the prescribed Hom-hermitian level structure.

items.name: Smooth specialization with support comparison
items.statement: The smooth-model specialization maps, both ordinary and compactly supported, are isomorphisms for the admitted coefficients. In the nonproper case use Lan–Stroh Corollary 5.20; smoothness alone is not the proof.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Smooth basic-locus correspondence
items.statement: Sp-star parametrizes definite-signature objects, principal in odd rank and with polarization defect p² in even rank. Bp-star adds the isogeny α:A→A-star with p-kernel constraint and varpi λA=α∨λ-star α, giving Sp-star←Bp-star→Mp.

items.statement: Choose the definite hermitian space V-star with the source’s away-p identifications and p-lattice discriminant; the definite moduli set identifies with Sh(V-star,K-star)×T. The identification retains these choices.

items.statement: Under §5.1’s definite tame hermitian datum and special inert p, Mp parametrizes the same signature but a polarization whose p-primary kernel lies in A[p] and has rank p². Its generic indefinite hermitian identification requires a separate uniformization datum.

items.name: Semistable nearby specialization
items.statement: Both ordinary and compact-support generic-to-nearby cohomology maps are isomorphisms; proper base change applies in the proper case and Lan–Stroh supplies the nonproper case.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Balloon isogeny resolution
items.statement: S° parametrizes the definite principal-polarization objects; B° adds β:A→A° with λ=β∨λ°β and kerβ[p∞]⊂A[p]. Maps π°:B°→S° and ι°:B°→M° identify B° with M°.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

uses.how: Use the universal isogeny and projective quotient of de Rham data.

api.name: RankinSelberg.BalloonIsogenyResolution.data
api.statement: Use the universal isogeny and projective quotient of de Rham data.

api.name: RankinSelberg.BalloonIsogenyResolution.characterisation
api.statement: ι° is an isomorphism.

api.name: RankinSelberg.BalloonIsogenyResolution.compatibility
api.statement: The fibre π°^−1(s) is P^(N−1) in the paper’s quotient convention.

unitTests.name: RankinSelberg.BalloonIsogenyResolution.test1
unitTests.statement: A hyperplane in the de Rham vector space determines the inverse Dieudonné lattice.

unitTests.name: RankinSelberg.BalloonIsogenyResolution.test2
unitTests.statement: The universal polarization relation fixes the isogeny degree.

items.name: Balloon fibre and Fermat link
items.statement: Every geometric balloon fibre is P^(N−1); its intersection with M† is a smooth Fermat hypersurface of degree p+1.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Link normal bundle
items.statement: The normal line of M† in M•, restricted to a balloon projective fibre, is O(−(p+1)); the balloon normal has the opposite degree.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Ground isogeny correspondence
items.statement: S• has definite signature and is p-principal for even N and defect p² for odd N. B• adds γ:A→A• with varpi λ=γ∨λ•γ, p-kernel constraint and the two Hodge/radical conditions of Definition 5.4.2; it maps to S• and M•.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

uses.how: Use the two flags H2⊂H1 in the de Rham module.

api.name: RankinSelberg.GroundIsogenyCorrespondence.data
api.statement: Use the two flags H2⊂H1 in the de Rham module.

api.name: RankinSelberg.GroundIsogenyCorrespondence.characterisation
api.statement: The flags satisfy radical⊂H2⊂H1⊂H2-ann and H2⊂H1-ann.

api.name: RankinSelberg.GroundIsogenyCorrespondence.compatibility
api.statement: The Lie quotient is H1-ann/H2 in the source convention.

unitTests.name: RankinSelberg.GroundIsogenyCorrespondence.test1
unitTests.statement: For even N the radical condition is automatic.

unitTests.name: RankinSelberg.GroundIsogenyCorrespondence.test2
unitTests.statement: For odd N the one-dimensional radical must be retained.

items.name: Ground fibres
items.statement: The π•-fibres are smooth projective DL• varieties of dimension floor(N/2), with pairing radical N mod 2.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Ground immersion and Lie bundle
items.statement: ι• is a local closed immersion; its normal bundle is (imγτ)⊗Lie(A∨)τc, and the pulled-back Lie line is H1-ann/H2.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Basic-locus coverage
items.statement: The basic locus is the union of the balloon/link and the image of the ground correspondence; for N≥5 it need not be equidimensional.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Link correspondence and uniformization
items.statement: S† parametrizes ψ:A°→A• satisfying varpi λ°=ψ∨λ•ψ. B† records the compatible factorization γ=ψβ. The link square over M• is Cartesian and S† identifies with the finite Shimura set at K†=K°∩K•, times T.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

uses.how: Use the factorization diagram and its universal property.

api.name: RankinSelberg.LinkCorrespondenceAndUniformization.data
api.statement: Use the factorization diagram and its universal property.

api.name: RankinSelberg.LinkCorrespondenceAndUniformization.characterisation
api.statement: Every geometric fibre over S† is P^(floor(N/2)−1).

api.name: RankinSelberg.LinkCorrespondenceAndUniformization.compatibility
api.statement: The map to the balloon fibre is a linear embedding and to the ground fibre is a regular divisor.

unitTests.name: RankinSelberg.LinkCorrespondenceAndUniformization.test1
unitTests.statement: N=2 gives zero-dimensional link fibres.

unitTests.name: RankinSelberg.LinkCorrespondenceAndUniformization.test2
unitTests.statement: The three isogenies must satisfy the polarization identities simultaneously.

items.name: Finite unitary level on the balloon
items.statement: Add a trivialization of A°[p] modulo the p-level congruence subgroup K°1. The quotient K°/K°1 is the finite unitary group, and balloon/link families become the associated projective/Fermat bundles.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

uses.how: Use the finite-unitary action and descent of the universal fibre.

api.name: RankinSelberg.FiniteUnitaryLevelOnTheBalloon.data
api.statement: Use the finite-unitary action and descent of the universal fibre.

api.name: RankinSelberg.FiniteUnitaryLevelOnTheBalloon.characterisation
api.statement: Forgetting level is the corresponding finite étale cover at neat tame level.

api.name: RankinSelberg.FiniteUnitaryLevelOnTheBalloon.compatibility
api.statement: The fibre representation descends via the same finite quotient.

unitTests.name: RankinSelberg.FiniteUnitaryLevelOnTheBalloon.test1
unitTests.statement: The full projective fibre has the expected hyperplane classes.

unitTests.name: RankinSelberg.FiniteUnitaryLevelOnTheBalloon.test2
unitTests.statement: Primitive link cohomology is a different representation from the whole middle cohomology.

items.name: Fermat cohomology away from middle
items.statement: With p+1 invertible in the coefficients, restriction from P^(N−1) to the geometric link is an isomorphism except in degrees N−2 and 2N−2.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Fermat integral freeness
items.statement: The admitted link cohomology groups are free over the chosen p-coprime coefficients. Integral middle freeness requires its own hypersurface cohomology argument.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Fermat middle Frobenius for descended forms
items.statement: For even N and an actual split Hermitian Fp²-model, middle cohomology twisted by (N−2)/2 has trivial residue Galois action. The general κ-form version requires this descent input (E9).
items.locator: Lemma 5.6.2(3), corrected scope of Lemma A.1.4(4)
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Primitive link cohomology
items.statement: Use the kernel of Gysin from degree N−2 of the Fermat hypersurface to degree N of P^(N−1). For N≥3 this agrees with the source’s cup-product primitive kernel; for N=2 use reduced H0, the kernel of total trace.
items.locator: Definition 5.6.3 and Appendix C.2, corrected E10
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

uses.how: Project away the ambient middle class with the required degree normalization.

api.name: RankinSelberg.PrimitiveLinkCohomology.data
api.statement: Project away the ambient middle class with the required degree normalization.

api.name: RankinSelberg.PrimitiveLinkCohomology.characterisation
api.statement: For N=2 the dimension is p, not p+1.

api.name: RankinSelberg.PrimitiveLinkCohomology.compatibility
api.statement: When p+1 is invertible, the ambient and primitive summands split with normalized projector.

unitTests.name: RankinSelberg.PrimitiveLinkCohomology.test1
unitTests.statement: At p=2 the three-point link has primitive rank two.

unitTests.name: RankinSelberg.PrimitiveLinkCohomology.test2
unitTests.statement: Cup product to H2 of a zero-dimensional scheme is zero and cannot define this primitive summand.

items.name: Primitive fibre automorphic description
items.statement: The localized primitive link cohomology is the automorphic function module with the corrected Tate–Thompson fibre representation; in even rank its local constituents are unramified-principal-series constituents, while odd rank forces the base-change pair {−p,−p^−1}.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Hecke isogeny strata for ground intersections
items.statement: For two S• objects classify φ=γ2γ1^−1 by the elementary divisor index j of pφ and its dual. Set Vφ=ker(pφ)/im(pφ^−1), of rank N−2j with inherited admissible pairing.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

uses.how: Use the kernel/image quotient and the finite Hecke fibre.

api.name: RankinSelberg.HeckeIsogenyStrataForGroundIntersections.data
api.statement: Use the kernel/image quotient and the finite Hecke fibre.

api.name: RankinSelberg.HeckeIsogenyStrataForGroundIntersections.characterisation
api.statement: im(pφ^−1)⊂ker(pφ), with ranks j and N−j.

api.name: RankinSelberg.HeckeIsogenyStrataForGroundIntersections.compatibility
api.statement: The quotient pairing has radical N mod 2.

unitTests.name: RankinSelberg.HeckeIsogenyStrataForGroundIntersections.test1
unitTests.statement: The intersection is empty for j>floor(N/2).

unitTests.name: RankinSelberg.HeckeIsogenyStrataForGroundIntersections.test2
unitTests.statement: At j=0 the quotient has the original rank N.

items.name: Ground intersection decomposition
items.statement: For j≤floor(N/2)−1 the relevant ground-fibre intersection decomposes into the indicated DL•(Vφ) pieces; the excess normal bundle is σ*H2⊗(H1-ann/H2).
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Link intersection decomposition
items.statement: The link-intersection pieces are projective spaces of dimension floor(N/2)−j−1 indexed by the finite isotropic choices; their excess bundle is σ*H⊗O(1), and the index count is the odd-power product ∏i(p^(2i−1)+1).
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Intertwining Hecke operators
items.statement: U=T°• and V=T•° are integral finite double-coset correspondences between the two special levels; I°=UV. Each Hecke algebra has unit 1K with its own normalization.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

uses.how: Use maps on finite Shimura functions and the two composites.

api.name: RankinSelberg.IntertwiningHeckeOperators.data
api.statement: Use maps on finite Shimura functions and the two composites.

api.name: RankinSelberg.IntertwiningHeckeOperators.characterisation
api.statement: Transposition interchanges U and V under the counting pairing.

api.name: RankinSelberg.IntertwiningHeckeOperators.compatibility
api.statement: Convolution coefficients count the finite lattice fibres; distinct K-volumes must not be silently identified.

unitTests.name: RankinSelberg.IntertwiningHeckeOperators.test1
unitTests.statement: A delta function maps to the sum over its actual finite fibre.

unitTests.name: RankinSelberg.IntertwiningHeckeOperators.test2
unitTests.statement: Odd-rank special subgroups can have different volumes.

items.name: Balloon, ground and link incidence maps
items.statement: Construct the three push–pull/Gysin incidence pairs with the powers of the projective hyperplane class of Construction 5.8.3. Set the link pair to zero in N=2 where its naive degree would be negative.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

uses.how: Read each cohomological degree and Tate twist before composing.

api.name: RankinSelberg.BalloonGroundAndLinkIncidenceMaps.data
api.statement: Read each cohomological degree and Tate twist before composing.

api.name: RankinSelberg.BalloonGroundAndLinkIncidenceMaps.characterisation
api.statement: The maps are adjoint under Poincaré duality and counting pairings.

api.name: RankinSelberg.BalloonGroundAndLinkIncidenceMaps.compatibility
api.statement: The N=2 convention removes the negative-degree link contribution.

unitTests.name: RankinSelberg.BalloonGroundAndLinkIncidenceMaps.test1
unitTests.statement: The odd-rank ground matrix acts in a single middle degree.

unitTests.name: RankinSelberg.BalloonGroundAndLinkIncidenceMaps.test2
unitTests.statement: The even-rank matrix needs an intervening first Chern class.

items.name: Odd incidence matrix
items.statement: For N=2r+1, the link/ground incidence composition matrix is [[−(p+1)²,U],[V,T•]], with T•=Σδ d•_(r−δ,p)T•δ.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Line-bundle incidence map
items.statement: For N=2r, r≥2 and a line bundle L on the ground tower, insert cup c1(L) between the incidence push and pull maps to obtain incL.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

uses.how: Use c1(L) to shift degree by two and twist by one.

api.name: RankinSelberg.LineBundleIncidenceMap.data
api.statement: Use c1(L) to shift degree by two and twist by one.

api.name: RankinSelberg.LineBundleIncidenceMap.characterisation
api.statement: c1(L⊗L′)=c1(L)+c1(L′) gives additivity of incL.

api.name: RankinSelberg.LineBundleIncidenceMap.compatibility
api.statement: Pullback of compatible tower line bundles commutes with level changes.

unitTests.name: RankinSelberg.LineBundleIncidenceMap.test1
unitTests.statement: The trivial line bundle gives zero incidence map.

unitTests.name: RankinSelberg.LineBundleIncidenceMap.test2
unitTests.statement: Tensor powers multiply the matrix by the exponent.

items.name: Even link-divisor incidence matrix
items.statement: For L=O(M†) the matrix is [[(p+1)^3,−(p+1)U],[−(p+1)V,R•]], where R•=Σδ=0..r−1 ((1−(−p)^(r−δ))/(p+1))∏i=1..r−δ(p^(2i−1)+1)T•δ. The product repairs E6.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Even Lie-line incidence matrix
items.statement: For L=LieA,τc the matrix is [[−(p+1)²,U],[V,T•]]. At intersection index j the excess Chern class has index r−j−1, as required by dimension (E7).
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Weight spectral sequence
items.statement: For the semistable model, E1^(a,b)=⊕i≥max(0,−a) H^(b−2i)(M^(a+2i),L(r−i)); differentials are the signed restriction and Gysin maps. The two-component model has columns −1,0,1.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

uses.how: Use the fixed component order and the monodromy map induced by identity on common link terms.

api.name: RankinSelberg.WeightSpectralSequence.data
api.statement: Use the fixed component order and the monodromy map induced by identity on common link terms.

api.name: RankinSelberg.WeightSpectralSequence.characterisation
api.statement: The restriction and Gysin anticommutation gives d1²=0.

api.name: RankinSelberg.WeightSpectralSequence.compatibility
api.statement: Changing component order transports the complex with signs, not by an unsigned identity.

unitTests.name: RankinSelberg.WeightSpectralSequence.test1
unitTests.statement: No triple intersection gives zero columns outside −1,0,1.

unitTests.name: RankinSelberg.WeightSpectralSequence.test2
unitTests.statement: For two curves, the maps reduce to graph incidence and its transpose.

items.name: Even weight sequence degeneration
items.statement: For N=2r, the source’s parity vanishing on balloon and link makes the weight sequence degenerate at E2.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Three monodromy graded pieces
items.statement: For N=2r the increasing filtration has gr−1=coker(d_res), gr0=H^(2r−1)(M•,L(r)), gr1=ker(d_Gysin), with monodromy induced by the identity on link cohomology.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Lowest inertia-cohomology piece
items.statement: F−1 H1(I,H^(2r−1)) identifies with (coker monodromy)(−1), equivalently im(d_Gysin)/im(d_Gysin d_res(−1)).
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Residue invariants exact sequence: missing boundary vanishing
items.statement: The source’s short exact sequence in Lemma 5.9.3(6) needs vanishing of the connecting map from ground-middle invariants to H1(Gκ,F−1H1(I,−)). The latter group is not generally zero merely because p²−1 is a unit. Retain the long exact sequence until the connecting-map assertion is proved.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.
items.proofStatus: open proof obligation; no unconditional Lean theorem proposed

items.name: Even potential-incidence matrix
items.statement: With a=p+1 the degree-changing three-by-three incidence matrix is [[a,a²,−U],[a²,a³,−aU],[−V,−aV,R•]]; for N=2 its link row/column vanish. Left multiplication by (V,0,a) leaves (0,0,aR•−VU).
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Odd Tate-cycle map nabla1
items.statement: On odd-rank E2 middle cohomology define nabla1=U(V Inc†*+(p+1)²Inc•*). The incidence relation makes it descend through d1 and factor through residue coinvariants.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

uses.how: Use the descended map and its finite Shimura-function target.

api.name: RankinSelberg.OddTateCycleMapNabla1.data
api.statement: Use the descended map and its finite Shimura-function target.

api.name: RankinSelberg.OddTateCycleMapNabla1.characterisation
api.statement: The expression kills im d1 by the odd incidence relation.

api.name: RankinSelberg.OddTateCycleMapNabla1.compatibility
api.statement: It is Hecke equivariant and factors through the stated coinvariants.

unitTests.name: RankinSelberg.OddTateCycleMapNabla1.test1
unitTests.statement: The relation (0,V,(p+1)²) times the odd matrix kills the differential vector (p+1,−1,0).

unitTests.name: RankinSelberg.OddTateCycleMapNabla1.test2
unitTests.statement: Dropping (p+1)² changes that relation.

items.name: Even level-raising map nabla0
items.statement: On ker d_res in degree 2r define nabla0=U(V Inc°*+(p+1)Inc•*). Its composition with the potential differential is controlled by aR•−VU.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

api.name: RankinSelberg.EvenLevelRaisingMapNabla0.data
api.statement: Read the restriction to ker d_res and the Hecke congruence quotient.

api.name: RankinSelberg.EvenLevelRaisingMapNabla0.characterisation

api.name: RankinSelberg.EvenLevelRaisingMapNabla0.compatibility

unitTests.name: RankinSelberg.EvenLevelRaisingMapNabla0.test1
unitTests.statement: Use a=p+1, not a², in the ground summand.

unitTests.name: RankinSelberg.EvenLevelRaisingMapNabla0.test2
unitTests.statement: Residually special parameters alone do not kill a higher λ^m quotient.

items.name: Special morphisms adjoining the CM factor
items.statement: The norm-one inclusion Vn→Vn♯ induces A→A×A0 on integral moduli, together with the auxiliary definite isogeny sets and special incidence correspondences in §§4.5 and 5.10.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

uses.how: Retain maps on all three strata and the auxiliary level object Ksp.

api.name: RankinSelberg.SpecialMorphismsAdjoiningTheCmFactor.data
api.statement: Retain maps on all three strata and the auxiliary level object Ksp.

api.name: RankinSelberg.SpecialMorphismsAdjoiningTheCmFactor.characterisation
api.statement: The smooth basic square is Cartesian when n is even; the semistable ground square is Cartesian when n is odd.

api.name: RankinSelberg.SpecialMorphismsAdjoiningTheCmFactor.compatibility
api.statement: The other parity must use the stated special DL morphism and finite degree p+1, not a false Cartesian square.

unitTests.name: RankinSelberg.SpecialMorphismsAdjoiningTheCmFactor.test2
unitTests.statement: The map from the finer Ksp Shimura set goes to the coarser Kn set.

items.name: Smooth special DL fibre morphism
items.statement: The special fibre morphism in §4.5 is an isomorphism when n is odd and a regular codimension-one immersion when n is even.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Ground special fibre morphism
items.statement: The semistable ground fibre morphism in §5.10 has the parity and regular-immersion behavior of Proposition A.2.3; for even n it is an isomorphism.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Second geometric reciprocity
items.statement: For the smooth diagonal graph and external basic incidence, the specialized graph pairing is transformed into the finite definite graph distribution by the odd Hecke operator T-star, precisely as the pull–push identity of Theorem 4.6.2. The choice-dependent identifications are transported throughout.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Semistable resolution of the product
items.statement: Let P=Mn0×T Mn1. Blow up its balloon×balloon stratum to obtain Q. Fix the cyclic order of its four components; retain the diagonal graph cycle and its strict/special transforms.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

uses.how: Use the blowup map σ:Q→P and the ordered stratum inclusions.

api.name: RankinSelberg.SemistableResolutionOfTheProduct.data
api.statement: Use the blowup map σ:Q→P and the ordered stratum inclusions.

api.name: RankinSelberg.SemistableResolutionOfTheProduct.characterisation
api.statement: Q is strictly semistable of relative dimension 2n−1.

api.name: RankinSelberg.SemistableResolutionOfTheProduct.compatibility
api.statement: The diagonal components are blowups along link×link; off-diagonal components are unchanged.

unitTests.name: RankinSelberg.SemistableResolutionOfTheProduct.test1
unitTests.statement: The special fibre has four components, five double strata and two triple strata.

unitTests.name: RankinSelberg.SemistableResolutionOfTheProduct.test2
unitTests.statement: No quadruple intersection contributes to the spectral sequence.

items.name: Exceptional link bundle and cohomology
items.statement: The exceptional double stratum is the projectivization of the rank-two normal bundle along link×link, with its two distinguished sections. Use the projective-bundle cohomology formula. A global trivialization is an additional claim, not supplied by the local blowup computation; see open investigation U1.
items.note: The printed trivial-P1 claim remains under investigation; this item uses only the canonical projective bundle, and the report explains the global normal-bundle obstruction.

items.name: Blowup cohomology
items.statement: Pullback into each diagonal blowup is injective and splits with the exceptional Gysin image of H^(i−2)(P††,O(−1)); off-diagonal pullback is an isomorphism.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Product incidence map nabla
items.statement: Form the four external incidence pairs indexed °†,°•,•†,•• and combine their pullbacks with coefficients I0I1, (p+1)²I0U1, (p+1)U0I1, (p+1)³U0U1 respectively.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

api.name: RankinSelberg.ProductIncidenceMapNabla.data
api.statement: Use the explicit sum on the correct degree of the four blowup strata.

api.name: RankinSelberg.ProductIncidenceMapNabla.characterisation
api.statement: The construction is compatible with the Hecke action and component identifications.

api.name: RankinSelberg.ProductIncidenceMapNabla.compatibility
api.statement: The differential cancellation uses both parity incidence identities.

unitTests.statement: Each summand lands in the same finite Shimura tensor module.

unitTests.name: RankinSelberg.ProductIncidenceMapNabla.test2
unitTests.statement: The exponent of p+1 differs between the four summands.

items.name: First geometric reciprocity
items.statement: The specialized diagonal cycle pairs with ground/link incidence through the two finite-graph Hecke distributions of Theorem 5.11.5; combining them by the odd intertwiner identity gives the I°even⊗T°odd finite period.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Level-raising prime of depth m
items.statement: For fixed Π0,Π1 and m, p satisfies (P1) exclusion of Σ; (P2) ell∤p(p²−1); (P3) QpΦ=Qp²; (P4) the even Satake parameter is level-raising modulo λ^m and the odd one is Tate-generic residually; (P5) both are intertwining-generic residually; (P6) the specified even Hecke quotient is unchanged by omitting the p-operators.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

uses.how: Project all six conditions, keeping the depth in P4.

items.name: Integral invertibility of intertwiners
items.statement: Under P5 the two compositions are Hecke units, so U and V induce inverse isomorphisms up to these units on the localized finite Shimura modules.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Compactly supported and ordinary comparison
items.statement: Under residual absolute irreducibility, the localized boundary cohomology vanishes and compactly supported cohomology maps isomorphically to ordinary cohomology. The proof uses the boundary automorphic description and exclusion of noncuspidal base change.
items.note: Boundary proof requires the cited original compactification and base-change inputs; this is not a general properness assertion.

items.name: Odd Tate-cycle surjectivity
items.statement: For N=2r+1 and the P hypotheses, nabla1 surjects onto the localized finite Shimura module.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Odd Tate-cycle isomorphism
items.statement: With the additional middle-cohomology hypotheses and Hypothesis 3.2.10, the relevant Frobenius module is weakly semisimple and nabla1 identifies its residue coinvariants with the finite Shimura module.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Even incidence surjectivity and torsion obstruction
items.statement: For N=2r the degree 2r−2 incidence map is an isomorphism and its dual degree 2r map is surjective; the latter kernel is the corresponding ground-cohomology torsion. The resulting nabla0 map is surjective, with the same obstruction in the singular comparison.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Rigid polarized deformation condition
items.statement: Fix residual polarization and multiplier η^N eps^(1−N), minimal ramification at Σmin, the exact special two-eigenvalue block at Σlr, regular Fontaine–Laffaille condition at ell and no ramification elsewhere. Rigidity fixes the specified local lifting components.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Even torsion-free ground cohomology
items.statement: Assume ell≥2(N+1), ell unramified in F, rigidity, absolute irreducibility over F(ζell), cohomological genericity and a nonzero localized finite Shimura module. Then the ground cohomology is free and the three E2 pieces are free.

items.name: Ground Frobenius exclusions
items.statement: Under R09’s hypotheses, ground middle cohomology has neither 1 nor p² as a generalized Frobenius eigenvalue.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Integral arithmetic level raising
items.statement: Under R09’s hypotheses and the depth-m P conditions, nabla0 identifies the specified singular cohomology modulo λ^m with the finite Shimura Hecke quotient. The localized geometric representation is a finite direct sum of copies of the conjugate residual Galois representation at depth m.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Mixed deformation crossing
items.statement: The local mixed deformation ring has a node x(s−p^(−2r))=0; define Runr=Rmix/(x), Rram=Rmix/(s−p^(−2r)) and Rcong=Rmix/(x,s−p^(−2r)). The global rings retain the other fixed local conditions.

items.name: Rigid unitary R=T input
items.statement: Under [51] Theorem 3.6.3 hypotheses D0–D4, nonzero localized Hecke algebra, ell≥2(N+1), residual absolute irreducibility over F(ζell), rigidity and middle-only cohomology at all levels, the global deformation ring maps isomorphically to the Hecke algebra, is a complete intersection, and the middle cohomology is free over it. D0 includes the weight-width bound and ell unramified in F; Σlr is empty when N is odd.
items.note: The original theorem and its proof were read. Adequacy, Taylor–Wiles complexes and Carayol input proofs remain explicit external gates.

items.name: Equal deformation-component multiplicities
items.statement: The free Runr finite-Shimura rank equals the free Rram Galois multiplicity rank. Use inertial rigidity and the normalized intertwiner trace formula of D.2.3, including transferability at bad places.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.
items.provenance: Continues cc-d67081 / PR #2181; published-version refinement by Codex codex-c83e7a.

items.name: Congruence comparison by finite cardinality
items.statement: The singular cohomology of the standard ramified block equals Rcong. After R14, the surjective level-raising comparison is a map between finite free Rcong modules of equal rank and therefore an isomorphism; transport through the Hecke depth-m quotient.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Conditional definite Ihara input
items.statement: Under the source’s weakened multiplicity-at-most-one spectral condition and ell∤p∏i=1..N(p^i−(−1)^i), the Tate–Thompson finite-type map in Theorem 6.3.5 is injective. This is a separate result and is not used to remove R=T from the integral proof.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: First reciprocity datum
items.statement: PI1–PI7 of §7.2 fix the inert prime, type and coefficient exclusions, even level raising at depth m, odd Tate genericity, both residual intertwining conditions, the two exact Hecke-quotient comparisons and tensor congruence. Also retain rigidity, both middle-free hypotheses, cohomological genericity and Hypothesis 3.2.10 in both ranks.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Product weight filtration
items.statement: Under X01 the localized nearby cohomology is concentrated in degree 2n−1, the product weight sequence has the three tensor-derived graded pieces and degenerates at E2; after twisting only the indicated upper piece can have Frobenius-fixed subquotients. The coefficient module is very nice in the sense of the potential-map theorem.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Potential differential
items.statement: For a proper strictly semistable scheme of relative dimension d over a henselian DVR with finite residue field and coefficients Λ=Qell or Z/ell^ν, form B^r=ker restriction on H^(2r) of components and B_(d+1−r)=coker Gysin in complementary degree, retain their E2-null subquotients, and take residue invariants/coinvariants to obtain A^r,0 and A_(d+1−r),0. The signed composite Gysin∘restriction induces Δ^r between them.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Nice and very nice coefficients
items.statement: Nice requires E2 degeneration and exclusion of fixed subquotients in E2^(p,2r−1−p)(−1) for p≠1. Very nice adds that invariants→coinvariants is an isomorphism for every subquotient of ker μ^(1,2r−1)⊕coker μ^(−1,2r−1)(−1).

items.statement: Under the original proper semistable and very-nice hypotheses there is an exact sequence 0→H1_ur→A_lower→Δ A_upper→H1_sing→0 in the precise degree 2r−1 and twist r.

items.name: Potential boundary equals Abel–Jacobi boundary
items.statement: Under the preceding hypotheses, the specialization class of a homologically trivial cycle maps through the potential cokernel to the singular localization of its étale Abel–Jacobi class. Apply the closure codimension condition when identifying the explicit specialized cycle.

items.name: Nonproper potential comparison
items.statement: For the actual product model use compactly supported equals ordinary cohomology and the source’s footnoted extension of the proper potential-map construction. The proof requires checking functoriality of supports, localization and the cycle specialization, not a blanket replacement of proper by arbitrary.
items.note: Original potential theorem read in full; the extension to this nonproper setting remains a named proof obligation.

items.name: First explicit reciprocity: quotient isomorphism
items.statement: The map nabla kills the potential differential modulo the even congruence ideal and induces the stated isomorphism to the even finite Shimura quotient tensor the odd localized Shimura module.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: First explicit reciprocity: diagonal period
items.statement: Under X01, pairing the singular Abel–Jacobi class with a finite Shimura eigenfunction equals (p+1)φ0(I°)φ1(T°) times its definite diagonal period, with the specified counting multiplicities.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: First reciprocity exponent equality
items.statement: Since the three factors in X05 are units under PI, the λ-exponent of the singular diagonal class equals the exponent of the finite diagonal distribution in the prescribed quotient.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Second reciprocity datum
items.statement: The good-reduction prime satisfies PII1,2,3,4,7 and the middle-free condition of Assumption 7.3.2. This list intentionally has no PII5 or PII6; retain the smooth special morphism and the odd Tate-cycle target.

items.name: Admissible coefficient place
items.statement: For Π=Π0⊗Π1 in ranks n0 even and n1 odd, λ is admissible when L1: ell>4n and unramified in F; L2: ell avoids Σmin; L3: the generic tensor is absolutely irreducible; L4: each factor is residually absolutely irreducible; L5: the chosen polarized lattices give restriction injectivity and GI(F+_rflx,T²−1); L6: the even factor is rigid with empty initial Σlr and absolutely irreducible over F(ζell); L7: both factors are cohomologically generic.

items.name: Elliptic examples have almost all places admissible
items.statement: For two geometrically non-CM and geometrically nonisogenous elliptic curves and the source’s modular symmetric powers, all but finitely many coefficient places satisfy admissibility. The argument uses large image, rigid deformation input and torsion cohomological genericity.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Steinberg–supercuspidal examples
items.statement: Under the very-special-prime hypothesis (Π0 Steinberg and Π1 unramified with simple eigenvalue 1), a supercuspidal place for each factor and F+≠Q, all but finitely many coefficient places are admissible.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Regular-unipotent tensor irreducibility
items.statement: For representations V0,V1 of the source dimensions with an element acting regular-unipotently on V0 and identically on V1, absolute irreducibility of each and the stated characteristic bound imply absolute irreducibility of V0⊗V1. The normal-closure argument in the report fills the invariant-subspace step.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Adjoint disjointness
items.statement: Under the full hypotheses and characteristic bound of Lemma 8.1.5, the tensor representation has no common irreducible constituent with its endomorphism representation. The proof uses the odd Jordan-block decomposition of the adjoint of a regular unipotent and Serre’s small-characteristic semisimplicity theorem.
items.note: Exact original Serre bounds and all constituent reductions remain an external closure task; no replacement by characteristic-zero reasoning is made.
items.proofStatus: open proof obligation; no unconditional Lean theorem proposed

items.name: Weight minus one
items.statement: The normalized tensor Rλ(Π0)⊗Rλ(Π1)(n) is pure of weight −1 and has the polarized duality required by the local finite-condition argument.

items.name: Integral change-of-level comparison
items.statement: At the permitted odd intertwining-generic primes the cohomological level-change maps are integral isomorphisms, uniformly over finite sets of such primes. Prove this using the integral Hecke-unit compositions, rather than inferring it solely from rational isomorphisms and freeness.
items.note: Source-specific statement; the common notation and coefficient conventions in contexts are part of this statement. No formalisation or proof closure is asserted by routing.

items.name: Nonzero definite period from central L-value
items.statement: For the relevant pair, nonzero central Rankin–Selberg L-value supplies a definite hermitian pair and finite-level Hecke eigenfunctions with nonzero diagonal period. Import the precise global Gan–Gross–Prasad theorem and its local compatibility conditions.

items.name: Conditional rank-zero Selmer theorem
items.statement: For the main adjacent-rank setup in contexts, assume Hypothesis 3.2.10 in both ranks, λ admissible and L(1/2,Π0×Π1)≠0. Then dim Eλ H1_f(F,Rλ(Π0)⊗Rλ(Π1)(n))=0. The source proof uses the lifting step E1; the extraction keeps that repair as an explicit gate.

items.name: Elliptic rank-zero corollary
items.statement: For the geometrically non-CM, geometrically nonisogenous elliptic pair and relevant modular symmetric powers specified in Corollary 8.2.3, nonvanishing of the central value L(n) implies vanishing of the corresponding Bloch–Kato group at all but finitely many ell. For n≥3 retain F+≠Q.

items.name: Very-special-prime rank-zero corollary
items.statement: Under the very-special-prime and supercuspidal assumptions of Corollary 8.2.5, and F+≠Q for n≥3, a nonzero central value gives the rank-zero conclusion for all but finitely many coefficient places.

items.name: Conditional rank-one Selmer theorem
items.statement: For the main adjacent-rank setup in contexts, assume Hypothesis 3.2.10 in both ranks, λ admissible and nonzero projected étale Abel–Jacobi class of the diagonal cycle. Then the tensor Bloch–Kato group has dimension one. The source proof’s exact diagonal-evaluation step E2 remains an explicit repair gate. Nonzero L-derivative alone is not a hypothesis sufficient for this theorem.

items.statement: DL(V,h) is empty if 2h<N+d or h>N; otherwise it is smooth projective of dimension (2h−N−d)(N−h), with the specified tangent Hom bundle. It is geometrically irreducible if 2h>N+d.

items.name: Fermat cohomology
items.statement: For nondegenerate V and h=N−1 the DL variety is a smooth Fermat hypersurface of degree p+1 geometrically. With p+1 invertible in the coefficients, its cohomology is free and agrees with projective-space cohomology outside the primitive middle degree; geometric comparison does not identify arithmetic Frobenius for arbitrary κ-forms.

items.name: Ground DL tangent filtration
items.statement: The ground DL variety is smooth projective, with tangent filtration whose pieces are Hom(H1/H2,H2-ann/H1) and Hom(H2/rad,H1-ann/H2). If d=N mod 2 it is geometrically irreducible of dimension floor(N/2).

items.name: Gaussian coefficient polynomial
items.statement: The Gaussian coefficient [a choose b]_q is the polynomial determined by the Gaussian Pascal recurrence, with value zero for b<0 or b>a and value one at b=0,a. Interpret specialization at negative q polynomially.

items.statement: For k≥0, Σδ=−k..k q^(δ²)[2k,k−δ]_(−q)=∏i=1..k(q^(2i−1)+1), as a polynomial identity.

items.name: Hermitian isotropic counting
items.statement: In a split nondegenerate Hermitian space of dimension 2r+ε over Fq², ε∈{0,1}, fix a maximal isotropic r-plane W. The number of maximal isotropic W′ with dim(W∩W′)=r−s is q^(s(s+2ε))[r,s]_(q²). The graph-and-trace proof applies also in characteristic two.

sourceIssues.locator: Lemma 2.6.4, p.134; published Inventiones 228 (2022), NSF PDF SHA-256 dd821abd…ec89d97
sourceIssues.correction: Require a compatible norm/power lifting assertion in the Galois closure; prime-to-ell order of γ alone does not imply it. The main GI(T²−1) setting needs its own repair and is not refuted by this example.
sourceIssues.reason: Take F+=Q(√5), F=F+(i), ell=3, m=1, R=Z3(1), j=2 and the identity polarization (muΦ=1). Let u=(1+√5)/2 and S be its one-dimensional mod-3 Kummer class, coming from the integral finite unit class. F(m)=F(m)+=F(ζ3); its degree over F+ is four, so u remains a noncube (use the fundamental-unit description of Q(√5)). FS=F(m)(cuberoot(u)) has cyclic cubic kernel. Choose γ induced by complex conjugation, of order two; hγ=1. Complex conjugation fixes the real cuberoot and inverts ζ3, so every lift of γ has square one. All associated-prime evaluations are consequently zero, while the right side is the full cubic kernel. The Kummer/Bloch–Kato unit identification is an explicit external input to this arithmetic witness, not claimed newly formalized.

sourceIssues.reason: Over O/λ^m with m>4, A=[[λ,1],[0,λ]] has image containing λ²O² and hence λ⁴O². Its total image has index |k|² but its two coordinate projections have indices 1 and |k|; a diagonal matrix with those projections would have index |k|. Right multiplication by a basis change preserves the image, so cannot diagonalize it. Thus the claimed implication from Definition 2.6.5 is false for general linear maps. This example is not presented as a realized Selmer evaluation system, so the finding is a proof gap rather than a counterexample under every global hypothesis.

openInvestigations.claim: Global triviality of the exceptional P1-bundle
openInvestigations.analysis: The local blowup gives P(N1⊕N2) with two sections; two sections do not imply triviality. A restriction of the two normal line bundles along a fixed-link-point × Fermat curve suggests O⊕O(p+1), a nontrivial ruled surface. The global identification for the actual moduli bundle has not been completed, so this remains an investigation, not an error finding. Projective-bundle cohomology still applies.
The finer Ksp level ordinarily maps to the coarser Kn level. The printed arrow and all identifications need page-image collation before an erratum is asserted.
